tips: Size: Kori Bustard is huge, turkey-sized or bigger; Red-crested Korhaan is a small, chicken-sized bustard.
Back: Red-crested Korhaan has bold cream V-shaped chevrons on its back; Kori's back is plain brown.
Belly: Red-crested male has a black belly; Kori Bustard's belly is white.
Head: Kori has a dark crest at the back of its head and a thick, finely barred grey neck.
Bill: Red-billed Oxpecker's bill is all red; Yellow-billed Oxpecker's is yellow with a red tip.
Eye: Red-billed Oxpecker has a bright yellow ring around the eye; Yellow-billed Oxpecker lacks it.
Back: Yellow-billed Oxpecker has a pale buff rump contrasting with its back; Red-billed's rump is plain.
Face: Black-collared Barbet has a bright red face and throat; White-eared Barbet has a white stripe behind the eye.
Belly: White-eared Barbet is dark brown with a white belly; Black-collared Barbet is pale yellowish below.
Face: Black-collared Barbet has a bright red face; Whyte's Barbet has no red, with pale face markings.
Back: Whyte's Barbet is dull brown with a pale wing patch; Black-collared Barbet is olive-brown.
Face: Black-collared Barbet has a solid red face; Crested Barbet's face is yellow speckled red.
Head: Crested Barbet has a shaggy black crest; Black-collared Barbet has none.
Call: Crested Barbet gives a long trill like an alarm clock; Black-collared pairs duet 'too-puddly'.
Face: Black-collared Barbet has a red face and throat; Acacia Pied Barbet has a red forehead and black-and-white striped face.
Throat: Acacia Pied Barbet's throat is black; Black-collared Barbet's is red bordered by a black collar.
Size: Acacia Pied Barbet is smaller and slimmer.
Face: Black-collared Barbet has a red face; Green Barbet has no red at all.
Back: Green Barbet is plain olive-green all over; Black-collared Barbet is brown above.
Habitat: Green Barbet is confined to coastal forest; Black-collared Barbet is widespread in woodland and gardens.
Head: African Fish-Eagle has a white head, neck and breast; Osprey has a white head with a dark eye stripe.
Belly: African Fish-Eagle's belly is chestnut; Osprey is white below.
In flight: Osprey has long, narrow, angled wings; Fish-Eagle has broad wings and a short white tail.
Call: African Fish-Eagle gives a loud ringing yelp, often in duet; Osprey is mostly quiet.
Face: White-eared Barbet is dark brown with a white ear stripe; Crested Barbet has a yellow face speckled red.
Head: Crested Barbet has a shaggy black crest; White-eared Barbet has none.
Call: Crested Barbet gives a long alarm-clock trill; White-eared Barbet gives harsh chattering notes.
Face: Crested Barbet has a yellow face speckled red; Whyte's Barbet is dull brown with pale face markings.
Head: Crested Barbet has a shaggy black crest; Whyte's Barbet has none.
Breast: Crested Barbet has a black breast band spotted white; Whyte's Barbet lacks it.
Face: Crested Barbet has a yellow face speckled red; Acacia Pied Barbet has a black-and-white striped face.
Head: Crested Barbet has a shaggy black crest; Acacia Pied Barbet has a red forehead.
Size: Crested Barbet is larger; Acacia Pied Barbet is small.
Call: Crested Barbet gives a long alarm-clock trill; Acacia Pied Barbet a nasal, repeated hoop.
Face: Crested Barbet has a yellow face speckled red; Green Barbet is plain olive-green.
Head: Crested Barbet has a shaggy black crest; Green Barbet has none.
Habitat: Green Barbet is confined to coastal forest; Crested Barbet is widespread in woodland and gardens.
Head: Wire-tailed Swallow has a bright chestnut cap; Barn Swallow has a chestnut forehead and throat.
Breast: Barn Swallow has a dark breast band; Wire-tailed is pure white below.
Tail: Wire-tailed Swallow's streamers are wire-thin.
Breast: White-throated Swallow has a black breast band; Wire-tailed Swallow has none.
Head: Wire-tailed has a chestnut cap; White-throated has only a small chestnut forehead patch.
Breast: Blue Swallow is glossy blue-black all over; Barn Swallow is pale below.
Throat: Barn Swallow has a chestnut throat; Blue Swallow has none.
Habitat: Blue Swallow is a rare bird of montane grassland.
Breast: Blue Swallow is glossy blue-black all over; White-throated Swallow is white below with a black breast band.
Throat: White-throated Swallow has a white throat.
Breast: Lesser Striped Swallow is white with heavy dark streaks; Blue Swallow is all glossy blue-black.
Head: Lesser Striped has an orange-rufous head and rump.
Throat: Barn Swallow has a chestnut throat and forehead; Pearl-breasted Swallow is white below.
Tail: Pearl-breasted Swallow has no long tail streamers.
Breast: Pearl-breasted lacks the Barn Swallow's dark breast band.
Throat: White-throated Swallow has a white throat; Barn Swallow's is chestnut.
Belly: White-throated Swallow is cleaner white below; Barn Swallow is often buff.
Tail: Barn Swallow has a deep fork with long streamers; Banded Martin's tail is square.
Throat: Barn Swallow has a dark chestnut-red throat; Banded Martin's throat is white.
Back: Barn Swallow is glossy blue-black above; Banded Martin is plain brown with a white eyebrow.
Breast: Banded Martin has a brown band across white underparts; Barn Swallow's band is blue-black.
Back: Rock Martin is brown all over; Barn Swallow is glossy blue-black above.
Tail: Rock Martin's tail is square with white spots when spread; Barn Swallow's is forked.
Habitat: Rock Martin hunts around cliffs and buildings.
Head: Greater Striped Swallow has an orange-chestnut cap; Barn Swallow's crown is blue-black.
Breast: Greater Striped is finely streaked below; Barn Swallow has a chestnut throat.
Back: Greater Striped has an orange-rufous rump.
Breast: Lesser Striped Swallow is heavily streaked below; Barn Swallow has a chestnut throat and no streaks.
Head: Lesser Striped has an orange-rufous head.
Back: Lesser Striped has an orange-rufous rump.
Belly: Rufous-chested Swallow is rufous below; Barn Swallow is pale.
Face: Rufous-chested Swallow's dark cap extends below the eye.
Back: Rufous-chested has a rufous rump.
Tail: South African Cliff Swallow's tail is square; Barn Swallow's is forked with streamers.
Back: South African Cliff Swallow has a pale buff-rufous rump.
Breast: South African Cliff Swallow has a mottled dark breast band; Barn Swallow has a chestnut throat.
Back: Grey-rumped Swallow has a pale grey rump; Barn Swallow's rump is dark.
Head: Grey-rumped has a grey-brown crown; Barn Swallow has a chestnut forehead and throat.
Belly: Grey-rumped Swallow is white below with no breast band.
Breast: White-throated Swallow has a blue-black breast band; Pearl-breasted Swallow has clean white underparts.
Head: White-throated Swallow has a chestnut forehead; Pearl-breasted Swallow has none.
Tail: White-throated Swallow has long streamers; Pearl-breasted Swallow's tail is short, without streamers.
Size: Pearl-breasted Swallow is noticeably smaller.
Back: Banded Martin is plain brown above; White-throated Swallow is glossy blue-black.
Head: Banded Martin has a short white eyebrow; White-throated Swallow has a chestnut forehead.
Tail: Banded Martin's tail is square; White-throated Swallow has streamers.
Breast: Banded Martin's breast band is brown; White-throated Swallow's is blue-black.
Breast: Greater Striped Swallow is heavily streaked below; White-throated Swallow is plain white with a dark breast band.
Head: Greater Striped Swallow has an orange-chestnut cap; White-throated Swallow is blue-black with a chestnut forehead.
Back: Greater Striped Swallow has an orange rump; White-throated Swallow's rump is blue-black.
Tail: Cliff Swallow's tail is square; White-throated Swallow has a forked tail with streamers.
Back: Cliff Swallow has a pale buff-rufous rump; White-throated Swallow's rump is blue-black.
Breast: Cliff Swallow has a mottled, smudgy breast band; White-throated Swallow's is solid blue-black.
Breast: Sand Martin has white underparts with a neat brown breast band; Rock Martin is brown below with no band.
Throat: Sand Martin's throat is white; Rock Martin's is pale rufous-buff.
Tail: Rock Martin shows white spots on the spread tail; Sand Martin has none.
Habitat: Rock Martin hunts around cliffs and buildings; Sand Martin over water and open country.
Tail: Rock Martin shows white spots when the tail is spread; Brown-throated Martin has none.
Belly: Brown-throated Martin usually has a white belly; Rock Martin is brown to rufous-buff below.
Size: Brown-throated Martin is smaller and slighter.
Habitat: Brown-throated Martin favours rivers with sandbanks; Rock Martin cliffs, rocks and buildings.
Wings: Sousa's Shrike has a white V on the shoulders; male Redback Shrike has none.
Back: Male Redback Shrike has a rich chestnut back; Sousa's Shrike is brown and finely barred.
Habitat: Sousa's Shrike is a miombo woodland bird.
Back: Lesser Grey Shrike has a grey back; male Redback Shrike's back is chestnut.
Face: Lesser Grey Shrike's black mask covers the forehead; Redback's mask barely reaches it.
Breast: Lesser Grey Shrike has a pinkish wash on the breast.
Wings: Lesser Grey Shrike shows a white patch on black wings; Redback lacks it.
Head: White-crowned Shrike has a white crown and forehead; male Redback Shrike's crown is grey.
Size: White-crowned Shrike is much larger and chunkier.
Behaviour: White-crowned Shrike moves in noisy groups; Redback Shrike is usually solitary.
Face: Male Redback Shrike has a black mask; Marico Flycatcher has a plain face.
Breast: Marico Flycatcher is clean white below; female Redback Shrike is scalloped or barred below.
Bill: Redback Shrike's bill is stout and hooked; Marico Flycatcher's is fine and thin.
Back: Southern Fiscal is black above with a white shoulder bar; male Redback Shrike has a chestnut back.
Head: Southern Fiscal's head is black; male Redback has a grey crown and black mask.
Tail: Southern Fiscal's tail is longer and black with white edges.
Tail: Red-tailed Shrike has a rufous tail; male Redback Shrike's tail is black with white sides.
Head: Male Redback Shrike has a grey crown; Red-tailed Shrike's crown is sandy-brown to rufous.
Back: Male Redback has a chestnut back; Red-tailed Shrike's is plain greyish-brown.
Tail: Magpie Shrike has a very long black tail; Redback Shrike's tail is short.
Back: Magpie Shrike is black with white wing patches; male Redback has a chestnut back.
Behaviour: Magpie Shrike lives in noisy groups; Redback Shrike is solitary.
Back: Lesser Grey Shrike has a grey back; Southern Fiscal is black above.
Wings: Southern Fiscal has a white bar on the shoulder; Lesser Grey Shrike has a white patch at the wing base.
Breast: Lesser Grey Shrike's breast is washed pink; Southern Fiscal's is white.
Breast: Red-capped Robin-Chat is bright orange below; Familiar Chat is dull grey-brown.
Wings: Red-capped Robin-Chat has blue-grey wings; Familiar Chat's are plain brown.
Habitat: Red-capped Robin-Chat skulks in forest undergrowth; Familiar Chat sits in the open on rocks.
Behaviour: Familiar Chat habitually flicks its wings; the robin-chat does not.
Belly: White-browed Robin-Chat is orange all the way down; Cape Robin-Chat's belly is grey.
Head: White-browed Robin-Chat has a black head and very bold white eyebrow; Cape Robin-Chat's face is greyer.
Call: White-browed Robin-Chat's song builds to a loud crescendo.
Head: White-browed Robin-Chat has a black head with a bold white eyebrow; Familiar Chat's head is plain.
Breast: White-browed Robin-Chat is orange below; Familiar Chat is dull grey-brown.
Habitat: The robin-chat skulks in thickets; Familiar Chat perches openly on rocks and buildings.
Head: Chorister Robin-Chat has no white eyebrow; Cape Robin-Chat has a clear white eyebrow.
Belly: Chorister Robin-Chat is orange throughout below; Cape Robin-Chat's belly is grey.
Back: Chorister Robin-Chat is dark slate above; Cape Robin-Chat is greyish-brown.
Habitat: Chorister Robin-Chat keeps to forest; Cape Robin-Chat is common in gardens.
Breast: Chorister Robin-Chat is bright orange below; Familiar Chat is dull grey-brown.
Back: Chorister Robin-Chat is dark slate-black above; Familiar Chat is pale brown.
Habitat: Chorister Robin-Chat lives in forest canopy; Familiar Chat in open rocky places.
Head: Capped Wheatear has a black cap and white eyebrow; Familiar Chat's head is plain.
Breast: Capped Wheatear has a broad black breast band on white; Familiar Chat is plain grey-brown.
Tail: Capped Wheatear has a white rump; Familiar Chat's rump and tail sides are rufous.
Breast: Cape Robin-Chat has an orange throat and breast; Ant-eating Chat is all dark brown.
Head: Cape Robin-Chat has a white eyebrow; Ant-eating Chat's face is plain.
Habitat: Ant-eating Chat perches openly in grassland; Cape Robin-Chat stays near cover in gardens and bush.
Back: Mountain Chat shows a white rump; Ant-eating Chat has no white on the rump.
Wings: Male Mountain Chat has a white shoulder patch; Ant-eating Chat has none at rest.
In flight: Ant-eating Chat shows pale windows in the primaries.
Head: Many male Mountain Chats have a grey or white crown; Ant-eating Chat is all dark brown.
Back: Ant-eating Chat is dark chocolate-brown; Familiar Chat is paler grey-brown.
Tail: Familiar Chat has rufous rump and tail sides; Ant-eating Chat's tail is dark.
In flight: Ant-eating Chat flashes white windows in the wings.
Behaviour: Ant-eating Chat stands upright on termite mounds in grassland; Familiar Chat flicks its wings.
Head: Whinchat has a bold pale eyebrow; male African Stonechat has a black head, female a plain face.
Breast: Male African Stonechat has a chestnut breast and white neck patch; Whinchat is buff below.
Tail: Whinchat shows white patches at the base of the tail sides.
Head: Spotted Flycatcher has a finely streaked crown; African Dusky Flycatcher's crown is plain.
Breast: Spotted Flycatcher has neat streaks; Dusky Flycatcher has a dull, smudgy grey-brown breast.
Size: Spotted Flycatcher is larger and paler; Dusky is small and darker.
Tail: White-tailed Crested Flycatcher fans a long tail with white sides; Dusky Flycatcher's tail is plain brown.
Head: White-tailed Crested Flycatcher has a crest; Dusky Flycatcher's head is rounded.
Back: White-tailed Crested Flycatcher is blue-grey and dark; Dusky Flycatcher is brown.
Behaviour: White-tailed Crested Flycatcher flits restlessly; Dusky sits still and sallies.
Eye: Cape White-eye has a bold white eye-ring; Dusky Flycatcher has only a faint pale ring.
Back: Cape White-eye is green above; Dusky Flycatcher is grey-brown.
Throat: Cape White-eye has a yellow throat.
Behaviour: Cape White-eye forages in busy flocks; Dusky Flycatcher sits alone and sallies.
Back: Ashy Flycatcher is blue-grey above; African Dusky Flycatcher is brown.
Face: Ashy Flycatcher has a dark line through the eye with white above it in front of the eye.
Breast: Ashy Flycatcher is pale grey below; Dusky Flycatcher is smudgy brown.
Size: Pale Flycatcher is larger and longer-tailed than African Dusky Flycatcher.
Breast: Pale Flycatcher is pale buff and plain below; Dusky Flycatcher is darker and smudgier.
Habitat: Pale Flycatcher favours open savanna woodland; Dusky Flycatcher forest edge and gardens.
Breast: Male African Stonechat has a chestnut breast and black head; Dusky Flycatcher is plain grey-brown.
Wings: African Stonechat shows a white wing patch; Dusky Flycatcher has none.
Habitat: Stonechat perches on grass stems in open grassland; Dusky Flycatcher keeps to forest edge and gardens.
Tail: Familiar Chat has a rufous rump and tail sides; Dusky Flycatcher's tail is plain.
Behaviour: Familiar Chat flicks its wings constantly; Dusky Flycatcher sallies for insects from a perch.
Habitat: Familiar Chat sits on rocks and buildings; Dusky Flycatcher in leafy forest edge.
Throat: Collared Palm-Thrush has a pale throat ringed by a thin black necklace; Kurrichane Thrush has black throat stripes.
Bill: Kurrichane Thrush has a bright orange bill; Palm-Thrush's bill is dark.
Eye: Collared Palm-Thrush has a pale eye.
Habitat: Collared Palm-Thrush lives among palms; Kurrichane Thrush in woodland and gardens.
Head: Male Short-toed Rock-Thrush has a pale whitish crown; male Cape Rock-Thrush's head is all blue-grey.
Size: Cape Rock-Thrush is larger and bulkier.
Back: Cape Rock-Thrush has a brown back; Short-toed's back is blue-grey.
Head: Male Short-toed Rock-Thrush has a blue-grey head with a pale crown; Familiar Chat's head is plain brown.
Breast: Short-toed Rock-Thrush is orange below; Familiar Chat is dull grey-brown.
Tail: Familiar Chat has rufous tail sides and flicks its wings.
Bill: Kurrichane Thrush has an orange bill; Miombo Rock-Thrush's bill is dark.
Head: Male Miombo Rock-Thrush has a blue-grey head; Kurrichane Thrush has black-and-white throat stripes.
Belly: Kurrichane Thrush has a white belly with orange flanks.
Back: Male Sentinel Rock-Thrush has blue-grey extending over the back; male Cape Rock-Thrush's back is brown.
Breast: Sentinel's blue-grey runs down onto the breast; Cape Rock-Thrush's orange starts at the upper breast.
Size: Cape Rock-Thrush is larger and heavier.
Breast: Groundscraper Thrush is white with bold black spots; Cape Rock-Thrush is plain orange.
Face: Groundscraper Thrush has bold black vertical face stripes.
Habitat: Groundscraper Thrush walks in open woodland; Cape Rock-Thrush perches on rocks.
Bill: Karoo Thrush has an orange-yellow bill; Cape Rock-Thrush's is dark.
Head: Male Cape Rock-Thrush has a blue-grey head; Karoo Thrush's head is dull grey-olive.
Breast: Cape Rock-Thrush is rich orange below; Karoo Thrush has a speckled throat and duller orange belly.
Wings: Orange Ground-Thrush has two white wing bars; Cape Rock-Thrush has none.
Face: Orange Ground-Thrush has black-and-white face marks; male Cape Rock-Thrush has a blue-grey head.
Habitat: Orange Ground-Thrush lives on the forest floor; Cape Rock-Thrush on rocky slopes.
Bill: Olive Thrush has an orange bill; Cape Rock-Thrush's is dark.
Head: Male Cape Rock-Thrush has a blue-grey head; Olive Thrush's head is olive-brown.
Throat: Olive Thrush has a speckled throat.
Habitat: Olive Thrush hops on lawns and forest floor; Cape Rock-Thrush perches on rocks.
Head: Male Cape Rock-Thrush has a blue-grey head; Familiar Chat's is plain brown.
Breast: Cape Rock-Thrush is bright orange below; Familiar Chat is dull grey-brown.
Size: Cape Rock-Thrush is much larger.
Behaviour: Familiar Chat flicks its wings repeatedly.
Head: Male Sentinel Rock-Thrush is blue-grey on head, back and breast; Familiar Chat is plain brown.
Belly: Sentinel Rock-Thrush has an orange belly; Familiar Chat is dull grey-brown below.
Tail: Familiar Chat has rufous tail sides and flicks its wings.
Belly: Common Bulbul has a yellow vent and pale belly; Southern Black Flycatcher is black throughout.
Head: Common Bulbul has a dark, slightly crested head contrasting with brown body.
Back: Common Bulbul is brown above; Southern Black Flycatcher is glossy black.
Face: Herero Chat has a white eyebrow and dark eye-stripe; Familiar Chat's face is plain.
Breast: Herero Chat is faintly streaked below; Familiar Chat is plain.
Behaviour: Familiar Chat flicks its wings constantly.
Size: Fairy Flycatcher is tiny; Fiscal Flycatcher is fiscal-sized.
Face: Fairy Flycatcher has a black mask and white eyebrow.
Back: Fairy Flycatcher is grey above; male Fiscal Flycatcher is black.
Belly: Fairy Flycatcher has a pinkish wash on the belly.
Behaviour: Cape Wagtail walks on the ground wagging its tail; Fiscal Flycatcher perches upright and drops to prey.
Back: Fiscal Flycatcher is black above (male) or brown (female); Cape Wagtail is grey-brown.
Breast: Cape Wagtail has a dark breast band; Fiscal Flycatcher is clean white below.
Wings: Fiscal Flycatcher shows a white wing panel.
Breast: Cape Robin-Chat has an orange throat and breast; Fiscal Flycatcher is white below.
Head: Cape Robin-Chat has a white eyebrow; male Fiscal Flycatcher has a black head.
Tail: Cape Robin-Chat has an orange tail with dark centre.
Wings: Southern Fiscal has a white V on the shoulders; Fiscal Flycatcher has a white panel in the wing.
Bill: Southern Fiscal has a stout hooked bill; Fiscal Flycatcher's is thin and flat.
Tail: Fiscal Flycatcher shows white panels at the base of the tail sides; Southern Fiscal's tail is longer.
Face: Angola Cave-Chat has a bold white eyebrow on a dark face; Familiar Chat's face is plain.
Breast: Angola Cave-Chat is boldly patterned; Familiar Chat is plain grey-brown.
Back: Breeding male Malachite Sunbird is metallic green; Cape Sugarbird is dull brown.
Breast: Cape Sugarbird is pale with a brown wash and yellow vent; Malachite has yellow tufts at the shoulder.
Tail: Male Cape Sugarbird's tail is far longer and floppy.
Breast: Male Orange-breasted Sunbird has an orange breast with a purple band; male Malachite is green throughout.
Tail: Male Malachite Sunbird has long central tail streamers; Orange-breasted's tail is short.
Size: Malachite Sunbird is clearly larger.
Back: Male Amethyst Sunbird looks black; breeding male Malachite is bright metallic green.
Throat: Male Amethyst Sunbird has an iridescent purple throat.
Tail: Male Malachite has long tail streamers; Amethyst's tail is short.
Breast: Male Southern Double-collared Sunbird has a red breast band; Malachite is green throughout.
Tail: Male Malachite has long tail streamers; Double-collared's tail is short.
Size: Southern Double-collared is much smaller with a shorter bill.
Belly: White-bellied Sunbird has a white belly; male Bronze Sunbird is dark throughout.
Tail: Male Bronze Sunbird has long tail streamers; White-bellied's tail is short.
Back: Male Bronze Sunbird is dark bronze-green; White-bellied is bright metallic green.
Back: Male Violet-backed Sunbird is violet above; male White-bellied Sunbird is metallic green.
Bill: Violet-backed Sunbird has a short, nearly straight bill; White-bellied's is curved.
Throat: Violet-backed's throat is violet; White-bellied's is green above a purple band.
Breast: Gurney's Sugarbird has a rufous-chestnut breast; Cape Sugarbird's breast is pale brownish.
Head: Gurney's Sugarbird has a rufous crown; Cape Sugarbird's is brown.
Tail: Male Cape Sugarbird's tail is much longer.
Size: Cape Sugarbird is much larger with a very long tail.
Breast: Male Orange-breasted Sunbird has a bright orange breast; Cape Sugarbird is dull brown.
Head: Male Orange-breasted Sunbird has a metallic green head.
Size: Cape Sugarbird is much larger with a very long tail.
Breast: Male Southern Double-collared Sunbird has a red breast band; Cape Sugarbird is dull brown.
Head: Male Double-collared Sunbird has a metallic green head.
Head: Breeding male Citrine Wagtail has a bright yellow head; Cape Wagtail shows no yellow.
Wings: Citrine Wagtail has bold white wing bars; Cape Wagtail's are faint.
Breast: Cape Wagtail has a dark breast band.
Belly: Grey Wagtail has yellow underparts, brightest under the tail; Cape Wagtail has none.
Tail: Grey Wagtail's tail is noticeably longer.
Breast: Cape Wagtail has a dark breast band; Grey Wagtail does not.
Head: White Wagtail has a white face and black crown; Cape Wagtail's head is plain grey-brown.
Throat: White Wagtail has a black bib; Cape Wagtail has a white throat and narrow breast band.
Back: White Wagtail is clean grey; Cape Wagtail is olive-grey-brown.
Back: African Pied Wagtail is black and white; Cape Wagtail is grey-brown.
Wings: African Pied Wagtail has a large white wing patch.
Size: African Pied Wagtail is bigger.
Face: African Pied Wagtail has a bold white eyebrow.
Back: Mountain Wagtail is clean blue-grey; Cape Wagtail is olive-grey-brown.
Tail: Mountain Wagtail's tail is very long.
Breast: Mountain Wagtail has a thin breast band on very white underparts.
Habitat: Mountain Wagtail keeps to fast-flowing forest streams.
Face: Karoo Scrub-Robin has a white eyebrow; Cape Wagtail's face is plain.
Tail: Karoo Scrub-Robin's dark tail has white tips and is cocked; Cape Wagtail bobs its tail up and down.
Breast: Cape Wagtail has a dark breast band; Karoo Scrub-Robin has a white throat.
Belly: Western Yellow Wagtail is yellow below; Cape Wagtail is white with buff flanks.
Back: Yellow Wagtail is olive-green above; Cape Wagtail is grey-brown.
Breast: Cape Wagtail has a dark breast band.
Back: Plain-backed Pipit's back is plain; Grassveld Pipit's is clearly streaked.
Breast: Plain-backed Pipit's breast streaks are faint; Grassveld's are bold.
Tail: Grassveld Pipit has white outer tail feathers; Plain-backed's are buff.

Breast: Tree Pipit has bold breast streaks fading to fine flank streaks.
Habitat: Tree Pipit prefers woodland; Grassveld Pipit open grassland.
Size: Bush Pipit is smaller and shorter-tailed than Grassveld Pipit.
Breast: Bush Pipit is streaked over the breast and flanks.
Behaviour: Bush Pipit often perches in trees and bushes; Grassveld Pipit stays on the ground.
Breast: Striped Pipit is heavily striped down to the belly; Grassveld Pipit's streaks are limited to the breast.
Wings: Striped Pipit has yellowish edges to its wing feathers.
Habitat: Striped Pipit lives on wooded rocky hillsides; Grassveld Pipit in open grassland.
Throat: Breeding Red-throated Pipit has a pinkish-red throat.
Back: Red-throated Pipit's back is heavily streaked with pale stripes; its rump is streaked too.
Breast: Non-breeding Red-throated Pipit is heavily streaked down the flanks.
Tail: Short-tailed Pipit has a very short tail; Grassveld Pipit's is normal length.
Size: Short-tailed Pipit is small and stocky.
Back: Short-tailed Pipit is darker and heavily streaked.
Back: African Rock Pipit is plain olive-grey; Grassveld Pipit is streaked.
Wings: African Rock Pipit has yellow-green edges to its wing feathers.
Habitat: African Rock Pipit lives on rocky grassy slopes and sings from rocks.
Back: Buffy Pipit's back is plain; Grassveld Pipit's is streaked.
Tail: Buffy Pipit has buff outer tail feathers; Grassveld Pipit's are white.
Breast: Buffy Pipit's breast is only faintly marked.
Tail: Mountain Pipit has buff outer tail feathers; Grassveld Pipit's are white.
Size: Mountain Pipit is larger and darker.
Bill: Mountain Pipit has a pinkish base to the lower bill.
Breast: Orange-breasted Waxbill is yellow-orange below; Common Waxbill is barred brown.
Size: Orange-breasted Waxbill is tiny.
Back: Orange-breasted Waxbill is olive with a red rump.
Back: Grey Waxbill is plain grey; Common Waxbill is finely barred brown.
Face: Grey Waxbill has a black eye-stripe; Common Waxbill's is red.
Tail: Grey Waxbill has a red rump and black tail.
Face: Black-faced Waxbill has a black face; Common Waxbill has a red eye-stripe.
Back: Black-faced Waxbill has a crimson rump and flanks.
Bill: Black-faced Waxbill's bill is dark; Common Waxbill's is red.
Tail: Breeding male Pin-tailed Whydah has very long black tail plumes.
Face: Common Waxbill has a red eye-stripe; female Pin-tailed Whydah has a black-and-buff striped head.
Back: Common Waxbill is finely barred; Pin-tailed Whydah female is streaked.
Belly: Common Waxbill has a red streak down the belly.
Breast: Blue Waxbill has powder-blue face and breast; Common Waxbill is brown and barred.
